hook: Sweep (掃) and remove (除) the dirt: that is cleaning.
犬 is 大 (big) with a dot, like a dog's ear. "Eee-noo!" the dog barks.
買 has 貝 (shell, old money) at the bottom: you pay shells to buy. "Ka-ching" sounds like かう.
食 is a lid over a food bowl. "Tah-bay!" you say as you sit down to eat.
Three (三) days (日), or the 3rd of the month. Say "mikka", not "san nichi".
Cold (冷) storage (蔵) building (庫): the box that keeps food cold, a fridge.
猫 has the animal side 犭 plus 苗. A cat says "meow", the Japanese cat is "ne-ko".
丈夫 is a tall (丈) grown man (夫): strong and solid, hard to break.
時 is sun (日) plus temple (寺): the temple bell tells the time. 3時 is three o'clock.
Same 時 (time) read とき: "at the time when", like 子どもの時 (when I was a child).
A big (大) person (人): an adult. Special reading: おとな.
A book (書) of words (辞): a dictionary.
The day (日) you were born (誕 and 生 both mean birth): your birthday.
夕 is evening, 方 is direction or time: the evening side of the day, late afternoon.
中 (middle) read じゅう means all through: 一日中 is the whole day long.
中 (middle) read ちゅう means in the middle of doing: 食事中 is during a meal.
頭 has 頁 (head) on the right. "A tama" (a ball) sits on your shoulders: your head.
兄 is a big mouth (口) on legs (儿): the older brother who talks loudly. "Ani" = big bro.
赤 grew from big (大) plus fire (火): the red of a big fire. "Aka" like a red "ah, car!"
Sound (音) that is fun (楽): music.
質 is quality or nature, 問 is to ask: asking about the nature of something, a question.
A big (大) change (変): very much, or a hard, terrible situation.
使 has a person (亻) on the left: a person you send to do a job, so to use.
雪 has rain (雨) on top: rain that falls frozen is snow. "You key" in the snow.
Buy (買い) things (物): shopping.
白 is the sun (日) with a ray of light on top: bright white. "Shiro" sounds like "show" white.
A big (大) strong man (丈夫) says: it's fine, I'm OK.
嫌 has woman (女) on the left. "Kill ray!" you shout at something you hate.
The stand (台) place (所) in the house where you cook: the kitchen.
誰 means who, plus か (some): "who-some", someone.
Every (毎) week (週).
読 has words (言) on the left: you take in words when you read. "Yo, moo!" says a cow reading a book.
前 means front or before: 駅の前 is in front of the station.
赤 (red, from big fire) plus い makes the adjective: red.
青 has life (生) on top: the blue green of young plants. "Ao" like a blue "ah, oh" sky.
昼 has the sun (日) in it: the time when the sun is highest, noon and daytime.
便 is handy or transport, 利 is benefit: easy to use and useful, convenient.
服 means clothes. "Fuku": you fold your fuku (clothes) every night.
青 (blue, green of young plants) plus い makes the adjective: blue.
酒 has water (氵) and a jar (酉): liquid from a jar, sake. お makes it polite.
強 has a bow (弓) on the left: pull a bow hard, strong. "Tsuyoi" sounds tough.
百 is one (一) on top of white (白): hundred. "Hyaku!" like a big cheer for 100.
色 is color. "Iro" sounds like "I roll" paint of every color.
魚 is a picture of a fish: head, body with scales, and tail (灬). "Saka-na" swims in the sea.
七 looks like an upside down 7 with a cross. "Shichi" (seven), also なな.
父 (father) with polite お and さん: your dad, said with respect.
A child (子) who is a woman (女): a girl.
Water (水) day (曜日): Wednesday, named after the water planet Mercury.
晴 has the sun (日) next to blue (青): sun in a blue sky, clear weather.
降 means to come down: rain and snow come down, they fall. "Fu-ru" like falling rain.
箱 has bamboo (竹) on top: a box made of bamboo. "Hako" sounds like "hack open" the box.
机 has tree (木) on the left: a wooden desk. "Tsukue" is where you sit and work.
開 shows two doors (門) being pushed open. You open (あける) something yourself.
忙 is heart (忄) plus lose (亡): so busy you lose your heart. "Isogashii" = so busy.
後 means behind or after. "Ushiro": the place at your back.
傘 is a picture of an umbrella: a cover with people (人) under it. "Kasa" keeps you dry.
Lower (下) hand (手): your hand skill is low, you are bad at it. Special reading へた.
休 is a person (亻) leaning on a tree (木): taking a rest.
年 means year: 三年 is three years. "Nen" counts years.
絵 has thread (糸) on the left, like an old picture woven in cloth: a picture. Just "e".
出 looks like a plant coming out of a box: to go out, to leave, to appear. "Deru" = exit.
隣 means next to. "Tonari" sounds like "to nearly" touch: the one right next door.
半 is a thing cut down the middle: half. 二時半 is half past two.
分 is a knife (刀) dividing: an hour divided into minutes. Sound changes: 一分 いっぷん, 三分 さんぷん.
Before (前) noon (午): morning, A.M.
洗 (wash) and 濯 (rinse), both with water (氵): washing clothes, the laundry.
Big (大) like (好き): to like something very much, to love it.
取 is an ear (耳) and a hand (又): in old wars soldiers took ears. To take or get.
薬 is grass (艹) over fun or ease (楽): plants that make you feel better, medicine.
会 means to meet: people come together under one roof. "Au": "ow!" when you bump into a friend.
奥 means the inside, the back of the house: the wife who runs the inner house. Polite さん.
Outside (外) country (国): a foreign country, abroad.
八 is two lines spreading apart, like eight's shape opening. "Hachi" (eight).
近 has the moving road part (辶): only a short walk away, near. "Chikai" = close.
A moving (動) thing (物): an animal.
黒 has fire (灬) at the bottom: the black soot over a fire. "Kuro" like a black crow.
A child (子) who is a man (男): a boy. 男 is field (田) plus power (力).
Cow (牛) milk (乳): milk.
Eat (食べ) things (物): food.
着 means to arrive or to wear. "Tsuku": the train arrives at the station.
Fire (火) day (曜日): Tuesday, named after the fire planet Mars.
生 (life, a young one) plus 徒 (follower): a young follower who learns, a pupil.
The week (週) before (先): last week.
楽 means fun or ease (also in 音楽, music). "Tanoshii": fun times!
飲 has food (食) on the left plus 欠 (open mouth): to drink. "Nomu nomu" as you gulp.
早 is the sun (日) just over the horizon (十): early morning, early.
九 is nine. "Kyuu" sounds like the letter Q: Q is nine.
九 (nine) read く: used in 九時 (9 o'clock) and 九月 (September).
This (今) morning (朝): this morning. Special reading けさ.
住 is a person (亻) plus master (主): the person who is master of a house lives there.
The month (月) before (先): last month.
Ground (地) drawing (図): a map. Read ち here, not じ.
冷 has ice (冫) on the left: cold to touch. "Tsumetai" like ice in a drink.
Every (毎) year (年): yearly. Both まいねん and まいとし are fine.
庭 has a roof part (广): the open ground by a house, a garden. "Niwa" for nice flowers.
六 looks like a little person with a hat and two legs. "Roku": six rocks.
甘 is a mouth holding something (the line inside) to taste: sweet. "Amai": "ah, my!" so sweet.
重 means heavy (also in 体重, body weight). "Omoi": "oh, my!" this bag is heavy.
玄 (deep, dark) plus 関 (gate, barrier): the gate area where you take off shoes, the entrance.
違 has the road part (辶): going a different way, so different or wrong. "Chigau": nope!
Drink (飲み) things (物): drinks.
乗 means to ride or get on. "Noru": "no room" on the train, but you get on anyway.
Half (半) part (分): half.
Mail (郵便) office (局): the post office.
妹 is woman (女) plus not yet (未): a girl not yet grown, your younger sister.
鍵 has metal (金) on the left: a metal key. "Kagi": the key goes "ka-gi" in the lock.
靴 has leather (革) on the left: leather shoes. "Kutsu": put your shoes on.
冬 has two ice drops (⺀) at the bottom: the icy season, winter. "Fuyu": "phew, cold!"
切 (cut) plus 符 (tag, sign): a tag cut and stamped at the gate, a ticket.
月 (moon, month) read がつ for names of months: 一月 is January.
入 means to enter: make something enter, to put it in.
菓 has grass (艹) and fruit (果): long ago sweets were fruit. お菓子 are sweets.
閉 is a door (門) with a bar (才) inside: shut it. You close (しめる) something yourself.
番 (number in order, turn) plus 号 (sign, number): a number.
短 has an arrow (矢) on the left: an arrow is short. "Mijikai": too short.
嫌 is the same kanji as in 嫌い (dislike). "Iya!" is what you shout: no, I hate it!
屋 means house or roof: a shop. 本屋 is a book shop, パン屋 a bakery.
歩 is stop or foot (止) over a second foot: one foot after the other, walking.
遠 has the road part (辶): a long road, far. "Tooi": so far you need two (too) days.
封 (seal) plus 筒 (tube, case): a sealed paper case, an envelope.
語 has words (言) on the left: words, language. 日本語 is Japanese.
教 means teach (also in 教室, classroom). "Oshieru": she shows you how.
風 is wind: steam blows like wind off a hot bath. お風呂 is the bath.
背 is flesh (月) under 北 (two people back to back): your back, then your height. "Sei".
飛 (fly) + 行 (go) + 機 (machine): a machine that goes flying, an airplane.
向 means to face: the place you face, over there on the other side.
肉 is a picture of meat with lines of fat. "Niku": meat.
横 has tree (木) on the left: a tree branch goes out sideways. "Yoko" is the side.
開 shows two doors (門) opening. あく: the door opens by itself (no object).
危 shows a person crouching on a cliff edge: dangerous! "Abunai!" means look out!
辛 is a needle for punishment: painful, so spicy hot. "Karai": like hot curry.
帽 has cloth (巾) on the left: a cloth cover for the head, a hat.
秋 is rice plant (禾) plus fire (火): fields burn red and gold at harvest, autumn.
起 has run (走) on the left: you jump up and get going, to get up.
暗 has the sun (日) on the left plus sound (音): you hear but can't see the sun, dark.
This (今) evening (晩): tonight. こんばんは means good evening.
Make (作) writing (文): an essay or composition.
雑 (mixed, all sorts) plus 誌 (record, magazine): a book of mixed stories, a magazine.
狭 means narrow. "Semai": "say, my!" this room is so small.
茶 (tea) plus 碗 (bowl, with stone 石): a tea bowl, now the rice bowl.
始 has woman (女) on the left: life begins with a woman, so to begin.
Every (毎) month (月): monthly. Both まいつき and まいげつ are used.
見 means to see: make someone see something, to show it.
Both (両) parents (親): your mother and father.
時間 is time (時) span (間): 二時間 is two hours of time. 二時 is just two o'clock.
橋 has tree (木) on the left: a wooden bridge. Careful: 箸 (chopsticks) is also はし.
置 has a net (罒) on top: put it down and leave it there. "Oku": put it, OK?
This (今) month (月).
This (今) week (週).
砂 (sand) plus 糖 (sugar): sugar looks like white sand. "Satou".
少 means few or a little (also in 少し). "Sukunai": not many.
Built (建て) thing (物): a building.
広 is a roof part (广) over a wide open space: wide, spacious. "Hiroi": a huge room.
文 (writing) plus 章 (section, chapter): a piece of writing, a sentence or text.
千 is ten (十) with a stroke on top: thousand. "Sen": a thousand cents.
右 is a hand over a mouth (口): the hand you eat with, the right. "Migi".
度 means degree or times: 三度 is three times, or 3 degrees.
熱 has fire (灬) at the bottom: hot to touch, also fever (熱). "Atsui": ouch, hot!
腹 has flesh (月) on the left: a body part, the stomach. Polite お plus なか (inside).
知 is arrow (矢) plus mouth (口): words as fast and sure as an arrow, to know.
速 has the road part (辶): moving fast on the road. Not 早い (early).
待 has a street (彳) plus temple (寺): wait in the street by the temple. "Matsu".
三 (three) plus つ: three things. Say みっつ, like 三日 みっか.
皆 means all: everyone, said politely with さん.
北 is two people sitting back to back: they turn their backs on the cold north.
姉 has woman (女) on the left: the woman who came first, your older sister. "Ane".
Outside (外) country (国) person (人): a foreigner.
切 (cut) plus 手: a small cut piece of paper you stick on letters, a stamp. Sound change: きって.
Older brother (兄) plus younger brother (弟): brothers and sisters.
切 has a knife (刀) on the right: to cut. "Kiru": the knife kills the string.
果 (fruit) plus 物 (thing): fruit. Special reading くだもの.
黒 (black, soot over fire) plus い makes the adjective: black, dark.
Red (紅) tea (茶): Japanese call black tea red tea, from its color.
立 is a person standing on the ground with arms out: to stand. "Tatsu".
Tea (茶) color (色): brown, the color of tea.
晴 is the sun (日) in a blue (青) sky: to clear up, to be sunny.
Two (二) days (日), or the 2nd of the month. Special reading ふつか.
留 (stay) + 学 (study) + 生 (student): a student who stays abroad to study.
卵 looks like two eggs side by side. "Tamago": egg.
鳥 is a picture of a bird with feet (灬) at the bottom: bird, and chicken meat.
番 means number in order: 一番 is number one, the best.
皿 is a picture of a plate or dish seen from the side. Polite お.
遅 has the road part (辶): slow on the road, so late. "Osoi".
覚 has see (見) at the bottom: what you see, you remember. "Oboeru".
返 has the road part (辶): send it back on the road, to return it. "Kaesu".
Yellow (黄) color (色): yellow. 黄 read き here.
万 means ten thousand. "Man": a rich man has 万 yen.
耳 is a picture of an ear. "Mimi": "me, me", I can hear you.
